payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_spec_citations.py::test_a_use_site_citation_is_left_while_its_definition_citation_is_rewritten stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'The held map read at the later commit, where no citation holds its construct, so nothing is rewritten.' applied to saffron/cli.py as an edit. The claim was "`citations_held_at(mirror, commit, text)` maps the offset of each citation held at `commit` to the name that held it. A name holds a citation when it opens exactly one construct there, and the range sits inside it or holds it whole. A citation that passes only by quoting a name on a line outside every construct is not held. Neither is one whose names open no construct, or one with no path, a missing file, a reversed range or a range past the file's end. None of those raises. So a moved definition citation is rewritten, and a moved use-site citation of the same name is left as a defect. A clause naming two names is held by one and rewritten only onto that name's construct. When two names hold it and one construct sits inside the other, the inner one's name holds it, in either clause order. Two disjoint constructs both held whole hold nothing, and neither do two of equal length. A name defined twice at `commit` holds nothing. The witness drives every member named here.", and only that witness ran under the edit.
